h1: Krabi Golden Hill Hotel — Budget Hotel With a Pool on a Hill Near Krabi Town
intro: If you're coming to Krabi on a tight budget but still want a pool to cool off in, free parking, and some peace and quiet while staying just minutes from town — Krabi Golden Hill Hotel is the name budget travelers keep bringing up in the Pak Nam area · It's a small 3-star hotel on a hill on Chamai Anusorn Road, only about 1 kilometer from the center of Krabi Town · Open since 2008, it has around 44 rooms, each with its own private balcony · There's an outdoor pool, a restaurant, a 24-hour front desk, free parking, and EV charging · The big draw is that it's one of the few budget stays in town with a pool at this price · Scored 8.1 from 16 Trip.com reviews · From about THB 700/night

body.html: Who Krabi Golden Hill Hotel is for — To put it as simply as possible, Krabi Golden Hill Hotel is for people who want a "budget stay that still has a pool and some peace and quiet" in Krabi, without paying beachfront-resort prices · It's not a luxury seaside property, and it's not right in the middle of the night market like many in-town hotels — it's a small hotel on a hill in the Pak Nam area that focuses on quiet, cleanliness, and value · Open since 2008, it has around 44 rooms, each with a private balcony · Real reviews on Trip.com, Booking.com, Agoda, and TripAdvisor all point in the same direction: this place suits budget travelers who still want a pool to dip into, couples who want privacy and quiet, small families who drive themselves and need free parking, and travelers using Krabi as a hub to catch boats and minivans out to the islands · On the flip side, if you want to step out of your room straight into a night market and restaurants, or you're after a beachfront resort in Ao Nang, this might not be the answer — its position on the hill means the surroundings are fairly quiet and you'll need a short ride or a bit of a walk to reach town · But in its role as a budget hotel with a pool near town, Krabi Golden Hill Hotel does its job well at a price that's hard to match, and the 8.1 score confirms that most people who arrive with expectations matching what the hotel actually is leave happy

Location and getting around — The location of Krabi Golden Hill Hotel is both a strong point and something you need to understand correctly · The hotel sits on Chamai Anusorn Road in the Pak Nam area, on a small hill, only about 1 kilometer from the center of Krabi Town · The good news is it's close enough to town to reach the center by car in just a few minutes, or walk in about 15–20 minutes if you don't mind the effort · Its hilltop spot away from the main road makes the surroundings quieter than a stay in the middle of the market, which people who sleep easily and like peace and quiet will really appreciate · Krabi Town has a night market, Chao Fah Pier with boats out to Poda Island, Chicken Island, and the Separated Sea, plus the bus terminal and minivan/bus connection points — all a short drive from the hotel · For getting further afield, Ao Nang Beach is about 30 minutes' drive away and Krabi Airport (KBV) is about 25 minutes' drive, and the hotel offers an airport shuttle (extra charge) and a tour counter to help sort things out · A point that comes up in real reviews is that there are no shops or restaurants right by the door the way there are at hotels in the middle of the market, because it's on a hill in a quiet area — so for food and getting into town you usually need to call a car or walk a bit · Anyone without their own vehicle should plan to use Grab or a motorbike taxi, and if you're relying on the hotel's shuttle, confirm the times clearly, since some reviews complain that the shuttle into town isn't always on schedule

"Loved that it's quiet and has a pool to dip into at this price · We drove ourselves so it was easy, free parking at the hotel, and just a few minutes' drive into town for the night market · If you don't have a car you might need to plan a bit for getting a ride since there are no shops right by the hotel"

Room types and decor — Krabi Golden Hill Hotel has around 44 rooms (about 39 of them air-conditioned), split into a few easy options based on group size and budget · There's the Standard Double Room (one large bed) and the Standard Twin Room (two single beds), the cheapest entry-level rooms, good for couples or a pair of friends who just need a clean place to sleep · Step up to the Deluxe Double Room and Deluxe Twin Room, which are a bit more spacious and tidier · A favorite detail for many is that every room has a private balcony to sit out and catch the breeze or hang laundry — something you don't often find at this price · Every room has air conditioning, a TV, a fridge, a kettle, a hairdryer, drinking water, free tea/coffee, and a private bathroom with a water heater · The decor is simple and practical rather than design-led, with no fancy touches · Many reviews agree the rooms are clean, more spacious than expected, and the beds are comfortable, which is why cleanliness scores around 8.2 · The honest thing to know is that the building has been open since 2008, so some of the decor and furniture is starting to show its age · A few reviews mention small details like a remote that doesn't work well, a burnt-out light bulb, or an air conditioner loud enough to rattle in some rooms · If you want a room in better shape, choose a Deluxe and ask for a recently maintained room when you book

Facilities and the pool — What sets Krabi Golden Hill Hotel apart from many budget hotels in the middle of town is that it has an outdoor pool · To be honest, the pool is fairly small — not a long lap pool for serious swimming, but plenty for a cool-off dip after a full day out, and a spot many reviews call clean and inviting · Having a pool at this price is a real advantage for families with kids or anyone who just wants to relax · Besides the pool there's an on-site restaurant with buffet breakfast, a 24-hour front desk that helps with late check-ins (handy if you arrive by car or boat late at night), free private parking which is a genuine plus for self-drivers, EV charging which is still rare at budget hotels, plus room service, luggage storage, a tour counter, and an airport shuttle (extra charge) · Wi-Fi is free in the common areas · Overall the facilities here punch "above their price" in offering a pool and EV charging, but it's still a small hotel with no gym or spa, so if you expect full resort-style facilities, set your expectations accordingly

Food and nearby places to eat — The hotel has an on-site restaurant serving simple dishes, plus a buffet breakfast (extra charge of about 120 baht for adults; some room rates don't include breakfast, so check when booking) · Some reviews speak positively about breakfast, saying it has both bread and Thai dishes to choose from and is reasonable for the price · But some say the breakfast selection isn't large, which makes sense given the size of the hotel and the price range · The honest thing to understand is that there are no restaurants or markets right by the door, because it's on a hill in a quiet area, unlike a hotel sitting across from the night market · So if you want to eat out, you usually need to head into town by car or walk a bit · The good news is that Krabi Town, only about 1 kilometer away, is packed with a night market, fresh seafood, rice-soup spots, coffee shops, and cheap local food · Many people choose to drive or call a ride into town for dinner, then come back to sleep in the quiet · In short, judged on hotel food alone it's decent and good value, but the real appeal for eating is in Krabi Town nearby, not at the hotel itself

Service — Service at Krabi Golden Hill Hotel earns fairly consistent praise in real reviews · The most-mentioned point is that the staff are friendly and helpful — many reviews use words like "lovely" and "ready to help," especially when it comes to recommending places to visit, booking boat tickets out to the islands, and helping call a ride · The 24-hour front desk also helps with late check-ins and travel information, making it easier for independent travelers to plan their next move · To be fair, some voices in the reviews reflect that responses to special requests sometimes fall short — like arranging a room as requested, or a shuttle into town that doesn't run on time as advertised, leaving some guests to call their own ride · This is normal for a small hotel at this price with a limited team · Overall, if you set your expectations to match the price and size of the hotel, the service here passes and is a point most people rate positively (service scores around 8.1)

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — Pulled together from Trip.com (8.1 from 16 reviews), Booking.com, Agoda, and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: a clean pool at a budget price, which is hard to find; rooms that are clean and more spacious than expected (cleanliness around 8.2); comfortable beds; a private balcony in every room; friendly, helpful staff; a quiet, restful atmosphere; free parking with EV charging; and value for money that many describe as "you get more than you pay for at this price" · On the watch-out side: the most-mentioned issue is the hilltop location, fairly far from shops and restaurants, meaning you need to call a ride or walk about 15–20 minutes to reach town, and the shuttle into town that isn't always on time · After that comes the air conditioner loud enough to rattle in some rooms, decor and furniture starting to age in a building open since 2008, small maintenance details like a broken remote or a dead light bulb, a breakfast selection that isn't large, and few international TV channels · Almost all of these complaints can be sorted by choosing a well-maintained room, arranging your transport in advance, and setting your expectations to match "a small budget hotel on a hill with a pool" — rather than being problems that keep people from returning · It's also worth saying honestly that the number of reviews on Trip.com is still small (16 reviews) and scores vary across platforms (TripAdvisor gives it around 3.4/5), so read the most recent reviews before deciding

"The room was nice and clean, with a balcony where you can sip coffee in the morning, and the staff were lovely and booked an island tour for us · The only downside is the air conditioner was a bit loud at night, and there are no restaurants nearby so you have to go into town to eat · But at this price, with a pool included, it's really pretty good"

Price comparison and value — Standard rooms start at about THB 700/night in normal pricing (I've seen lower during promotions or low season, with some platforms starting around THB 700–800), rising to about THB 1,000–1,400+ for Deluxe rooms in high season or on long weekends · Compared with budget stays in Krabi at the same level, what makes Krabi Golden Hill Hotel especially good value is having a pool at this price, which many budget hotels in the middle of town, such as City Hotel Krabi, don't have · Compared with a hostel in town like Pak-Up Hostel, which focuses on dorm beds and a social vibe, this place gives you private-room privacy with a balcony and a pool at a price that's still within reach · And compared with resorts on the Ao Nang side that start several times higher, this saves on both the room rate and gives you peace and quiet · But understand that what you "trade" is a location that's not next to the market or the beach, having to get into town yourself, and an older building with details that show their age · If you plan to drive yourself, want a pool to dip into, and like the quiet, every baht you pay feels well spent

What to know before booking — A few things help your stay go more smoothly · One, transport is the thing to plan most, because the hotel is on a hill about 1 kilometer from town with no shops right by the door — if you don't have your own car, be ready to call a Grab or motorbike taxi, and if you're relying on the hotel shuttle, confirm the times clearly since some reviews complain it isn't punctual · Two, if room condition matters to you, choose a Deluxe and ask for a recently maintained room, because the building has been open since 2008 and some rooms show their age · Three, check on breakfast when booking, since some room rates don't include it (about 120 baht/adult extra) · Four, if you're sensitive to AC noise, try asking to change rooms if you get a unit that's loud or rattles, since it's a frequently mentioned point · Five, if you drive yourself, the free parking and EV charging are a big advantage · Six, make use of the 24-hour front desk and tour counter for late check-ins, booking boat tickets out to the islands, booking tours, and arranging a ride to the airport or Ao Nang · Seven, in high season (November–April) Krabi gets busy, so book ahead, compare prices across several platforms, and pick free cancellation if your plans aren't firm · Eight, since the number of online reviews is still fairly small, read the most recent ones to check the current condition before deciding

The verdict — From everything real reviews say, Krabi Golden Hill Hotel is the best fit for people who want a budget stay in Krabi but still want a pool and some peace and quiet, especially those who drive themselves and use Krabi as a base for boat trips out to the islands · Having a pool, free parking, EV charging, a balcony in every room, and being only about 1 kilometer from town makes it good value that's hard to match at this price · But you have to accept honestly that it's on a hill away from shops and the beach, you'll need to plan getting into town yourself, and it's a building that's been open since 2008, so there are details around room condition and AC noise in some spots that come with age, plus a shuttle that isn't always on time · If you want to step out of your room straight into a market, or you're after a beachfront resort in Ao Nang, this isn't the answer and you should look at the town center or Ao Nang instead · But for a budget Krabi trip where you want a pool, quiet, and a spot near town on a light budget — Krabi Golden Hill Hotel is a well-balanced choice for the price and what you get, and it's the reason it still scores 8.1 from guests who come with expectations matching what the hotel actually is

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Krabi Golden Hill Hotel

faq.q: Where is Krabi Golden Hill Hotel · is it easy to get into town?
faq.a: The hotel is on Chamai Anusorn Road in the Pak Nam area, on a hill near Krabi Town, about 1 kilometer from the center · You can reach town by car in a few minutes, or walk about 15–20 minutes · Town has a night market, Chao Fah Pier with boats to the islands, and transport connection points · Ao Nang Beach is about 30 minutes' drive and Krabi Airport about 25 minutes' drive · Note that there are no shops right by the door, so if you don't have a car, plan to call a ride

faq.q: Does Krabi Golden Hill Hotel have a pool?
faq.a: Yes, it has an outdoor pool · It's a small pool for cooling off rather than swimming laps, but many reviews say it's clean and inviting · Having a pool at a budget stay is a genuine advantage here, since many budget hotels in the middle of Krabi Town don't have one

faq.q: What's the starting price at Krabi Golden Hill Hotel · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 700/night for a Standard room in normal pricing · There's Standard Double, Standard Twin, Deluxe Double, and Deluxe Twin to choose from, and every room has air conditioning, a TV, a fridge, a kettle, and a private balcony · Prices in high season (Nov–Apr) go up, so compare several platforms and pick free cancellation before booking

faq.q: Who is Krabi Golden Hill Hotel for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for budget travelers who still want a pool and some peace and quiet, couples who want privacy, and families who drive themselves and need free parking · It works well as a base for catching cars and boats out to the islands · If you want to step out of your room straight into a market, or you're after a beachfront resort, the town center or Ao Nang might suit you better

faq.q: Are there restaurants near the hotel · how do you get into town?
faq.a: There are no restaurants or markets right by the door, because it's on a hill in a quiet area · Most of the time you'll need to head into town, about 1 kilometer away, to find food — and there you'll find a night market and plenty of restaurants · Driving yourself is easiest; if you don't have a car, be ready to call a Grab or motorbike taxi · Some reviews complain the hotel shuttle into town isn't always on time, so confirm the schedule clearly

faq.q: Does Krabi Golden Hill Hotel have breakfast and parking?
faq.a: Yes, there's a restaurant and a buffet breakfast (with both bread and Thai dishes, though the selection isn't large, and some room rates charge about 120 baht/adult extra for breakfast, so check when booking) · For parking, there's free private parking and an EV charging point, which is an advantage for self-drivers
